Answer stability at temperature zero

Source: vignettes/llm-stability.Rmd
llm-stability.Rmd

The frozen public data from Atil et al.’s llm-stability repository contain 82850 calls across 5 models, 8 tasks and 10 runs. ANK-40 fixes commit c089c02ecfdb2a7fee0b321069a2d19cb8f11ae0, the Apache 2.0 licence and the complete v3 zero-shot selection. The model configuration uses temperature 0 and top_p_k 1. These are recorded historical calls; building this article makes no model calls and needs no external data.

The preparation script data-raw/make_llm_stability.R verifies the source hashes and the complete item grid before publishing the subset. SHA256SUMS covers the stored gzip file and its provenance. The archive contains other configurations, which are outside this selection.

What counts as an answer

The parser accepts exactly one distinct valid option label such as (A) in parentheses, ignoring letter case, with no spaces inside the parentheses. Bare letters, including the English words “A” and “I”, do not count. Repeated occurrences of the same label count once; different labels anywhere in the response, including quoted alternatives, make the answer ambiguous. There is no priority for a final sentence. For navigate, exactly one of the whole words “Yes” or “No” is required. The key never selects an answer. An empty, unparseable or ambiguous response remains missing.

correct compares the parsed label literally with the source key. A missing answer has missing correctness. The source also contains non-label keys:

Non-label answer keys: ruin_names item_id 99; ruin_names item_id 144.

For these ruin_names items, every parsed option label counts as a miss under literal label/key equality, even when its meaning matches the intended answer. The data retain that limitation; the keys are not repaired. Thus the hit rate describes this extraction rule, not a human reassessment of the response text. The provenance records parsing failures by reason, task and model. Raw response texts are not distributed.

Observed repeatability and hit rate

For each task and model, attribute repeatability is the fraction of items with a present, identical answer in every run. A missing answer breaks agreement. The hit rate divides the number of correct == TRUE calls by all calls, including missing answers. The missing-answer share is shown alongside both quantities. None of these denominators depends on a fit.

cells <- split(items, list(items$task, items$model), drop = TRUE)
rates <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cells, function(d) {
  answers <- split(d$answer, d$item_id)
  identical_answers <- vapply(answers, function(x) !anyNA(x) && length(unique(x)) == 1L, logical(1))
  data.frame(task = d$task[1L], model = d$model[1L], items = length(answers), calls = nrow(d),
    answer_repeatability = mean(identical_answers), hit_rate = mean(d$correct %in% TRUE),
    missing_answer_share = mean(is.na(d$answer)))
}))
rownames(rates) <- NULL

Binary variance components

Each task gets its own binary fit. Item is the question, model is the source model, and replicate is the original run number. The one prompt and one block level are constant. msa_counts() counts all imported calls, including those whose correctness is missing. The fit drops those missing responses, with its warning recorded below; it does not recode them as false. Fits use the default probit link and no interactions. Each fit and msa_grr() is recomputed here.

analyses <- lapply(unique(items$task), function(task) {
  d <- items[items$task == task, , drop = FALSE]
  runs <- as_msa_runs(data.frame(item_id = as.character(d$item_id), prompt_id = "task",
                                 model_id = d$model, rep = d$run, value = as.integer(d$correct)))
  counts <- msa_counts(runs)
  diagnostics <- character()
  fit <- withCallingHandlers(msa_fit(runs, type = "binary", interactions = FALSE, link = "probit"),
    warning = function(w) {
      diagnostics <<- c(diagnostics, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }, message = function(m) {
      diagnostics <<- c(diagnostics, conditionMessage(m)); invokeRestart("muffleMessage")
    })
  grr <- msa_grr(fit)
  components <- setNames(fit$vc$variance, fit$vc$source)
  list(counts = data.frame(task = task, counts),
    summary = data.frame(task = task, item = components[["item"]], model = components[["model"]],
      grr_pct_study_var = grr$summary[["grr_pct_study_var"]], observations = fit$n$observations,
      converged = fit$converged, singular = fit$singular),
    diagnostics = data.frame(task = task, diagnostic = if (length(diagnostics)) paste(unique(diagnostics), collapse = " | ") else "none"))
})

The latent residual variance is fixed by the link. It is not a measurement of observed disagreement between repeated calls; use the answer-repeatability table for that question. Large latent item components can accompany a flat likelihood, and missing responses can select which calls enter the model. The convergence and singularity flags describe the actual fit. AIAG bands on this scale are conventions, not evidence of correctness or suitability for another use. See vignette("validation") for engine comparisons and the simulation findings, including bias with few prompt or model levels.
